text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA

- Opposition coalition Zajedno no longer exists as an election coalition only as a deputy club in the federal parliament and at local level where it is in power said Zoran Djindjic, president of the Democratic Party one of the coalition partners.
- Serbian Renewal Movement President Vuk Draskovic accused Zoran Djindjic of leaving the opposition coalition Zajedno and cooperating with the Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Yugoslav monetary authorities said banks would start unlimited sale of hard currency at the official exchange rate of 3.3 dinars to the German mark by the end of the week.

- Yugoslavia's total debt to commercial creditors could stand at $2.25 billion after the expected conclusion of a separate agreement between Bosnia and the London Club of creditors on June 30, according to Merrill Lynch investment bank.
- University teachers will request an audience with Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic because of the critical financial situation of the Belgrade university.

- David Philips, chairman of the U.S. council for international affairs, proposed at a round table on Kosovo a series of confidence-building measures on the issue including an international conference, control of human rights violations, return of all refugees. Serbia should be asked to halt repressive measures and release all political prisoners and Kosovo to give up its notions of independence.
- Democratic Party President Zoran Djindic said a coalition with the Montenegrin Democratic Party of Socialists was possible at the federal level.
- Invalids of the last war will stage a rally on June 26 because the authorities have not yet started dealing with the problem of their unresolved status.
- Money supply is growing again and has exceeded six billion dinars, passing the December 1996 high, said the Belgrade-based Economics institute.
- Yugoslav Left is preparing to purchase a 49 percent stake in the Belgrade broadcasting and TV house Studio B through the Russian television NTV.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to visit Greece at the invitation of his Greek counterpart Kostas Simitis to discuss further strengthening of bilateral ties.
- Proposals to turn the daily Borba and the Yugoslavia official Gazzette into public firms from the presently socially owned firms was submitted to the federal parliament Thursday session.

- Seminar of young socialists which gathered a record number of young people shows that the left is in its full expansion now, said Zeljko Simic a member of the main board of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Belgrade's bank Beobanka and Greek Agrotiki Bank to sign an agreement on issuing bilingual savings books to Yugoslavs for dollar, mark and Swiss franks deposits that can be used in both Greece and Yugoslavia.
- The electricity network linking Yugoslavia to western Europe, interrupted in 1991, could be restored by end of year through Trebinje-Gacko-Mostar-Split and Rijeka.
- Some commercial banks announce they will sue the National Bank of Yugoslavia for unconstitutional insolvency closure.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- The Main Board of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists by majority vote supported the nomination of Slobodan Milosevic for the post of federal president with 56 votes for, 31 against and 10 abstentions. The board unanimously refused changes to the federal constitution proposing election of the federal president by universal vote.

- Montenegrin electricity company Elektroprivreda Crne Gore, worth $1.12 billion, will distribute 10 percent free shares to its workers. The company will privatise by a special government programme. It will issue a tender for concessions for the construction of hydro-electric power plants on the river Moraca. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
